title: Cross-Border and Group Supervision
summary: An eight-module programme on home-host supervision, consolidated group oversight, MoUs, supervisory colleges, third-country firms and cross-border crisis cooperation.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to supervise financial groups that operate across borders: working effectively as home or host supervisor, sharing information, participating in colleges and cooperating in a crisis.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors the frameworks and practical skills to oversee cross-border groups, branches and third-country firms without gaps or duplication. Participants leave able to assess group structures and intra-group risk, use cooperation arrangements and colleges effectively, and protect their own jurisdiction's interests in normal times and in a crisis.
sections.What It Covers: Home and host responsibilities, consolidated and group-wide supervision, intra-group exposures and complex structures, MoUs and information sharing, supervisory colleges, branches, subsidiaries and third-country firms, cross-border crisis cooperation, and overcoming obstacles to cooperation.
Intended Audience: Supervisors responsible for cross-border groups, branches, subsidiaries or third-country firms
International affairs, legal and cooperation staff managing MoUs and information requests
Senior supervisors and managers who represent the authority in colleges and crisis management groups
Learning Objectives: Explain home and host responsibilities under international standards such as the Basel Core Principles
Assess group structures, intra-group exposures and contagion risk on a consolidated basis
Evaluate MoUs and information-sharing arrangements and use them effectively
Contribute to joint risk assessments and coordinated decisions in supervisory colleges
Assess the risks of branches, subsidiaries and third-country firms in the authority's market
Apply cooperation principles to cross-border crisis management and resolution
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing on international standards with case studies and practical exercises, ending in a cross-border simulation, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of prudential or conduct supervision is helpful. No prior involvement in colleges or international cooperation is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IAIS, Insurance Core Principles and Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups (ComFrame)

modules.title: Foundations of Home and Host Supervision
modules.summary: Why cross-border groups need cooperating supervisors, how responsibilities are allocated between home and host, and the risks of supervisory gaps and duplication.
objectives: Explain the home-host principle in the Basel Core Principles and other sector standards
Distinguish home and host supervisor roles and responsibilities
Identify the risks of gaps, duplication and conflicting demands
syllabus: Basel Core Principles, IAIS and IOSCO standards on cross-border cooperation
Allocation of home and host responsibilities across sectors
Asymmetry: large home, small host and systemic branches
Supervisory gaps, regulatory arbitrage and duplication

modules.title: Consolidated and Group-Wide Supervision
modules.summary: Why supervisors look at groups rather than single legal entities, how consolidated supervision works, and how to assess group governance and risk management.
objectives: Explain consolidated versus solo supervision
Assess group governance, risk management and risk appetite
Identify perimeter issues in group supervision
syllabus: Common cross-border group structures across banking, insurance and investment
Scope of consolidation, holding companies and unregulated entities
Group-level versus entity-level governance and risk appetite
Financial conglomerates and cross-sector groups

modules.title: Intra-Group Exposures, Contagion and Complex Structures
modules.summary: How funding, guarantees and shared services link entities within a group, how stress spreads between them, and the supervisory risks of opaque or complex structures.
objectives: Assess types of intra-group exposure and dependency
Identify contagion channels within a cross-border group
Evaluate the risks of opaque or unnecessarily complex structures
syllabus: Intra-group funding, guarantees, liquidity and capital flows
Shared services, outsourcing and operational dependencies
Ring-fencing, structural subordination and trapped resources
Case study: assessing a complex cross-border group

modules.title: MoUs and Information Sharing
modules.summary: How information-sharing gateways and memoranda of understanding work, what a good MoU contains, and how to make and respond to cooperation requests effectively.
objectives: Explain information-sharing gateways and confidentiality constraints
Assess whether an MoU is fit for purpose
Prepare and respond to cross-border information requests
syllabus: Bilateral and multilateral MoUs, including the IOSCO MMoU
Confidentiality, data protection and onward-sharing limits
Making a clear, proportionate cooperation request
Exercise: reviewing a sample MoU for strengths and gaps

modules.title: Supervisory Colleges: Joint Risk Assessment and Decisions
modules.summary: How supervisory colleges are governed, how members build a shared risk picture across jurisdictions, and how to reach coordinated decisions and manage disagreement.
objectives: Explain the purpose, governance and outputs of supervisory colleges
Contribute effectively to a joint risk assessment
Manage disagreement and unequal engagement among college members
syllabus: College governance: chair, secretariat, membership and workplans
Building and reconciling a joint risk assessment
Coordinated decisions, constructive challenge and escalation
Case study: a college facing a coordination challenge

modules.title: Branches, Subsidiaries and Third-Country Firms
modules.summary: The supervisory trade-offs between branches and subsidiaries, how cross-border access and passporting regimes allocate responsibility, and how hosts assess third-country firms and equivalence reliance.
objectives: Compare the supervisory risks of branches and subsidiaries
Assess third-country firms and reliance on home supervision
Identify when a host should require subsidiarisation or additional safeguards
syllabus: Branch versus subsidiary: capital, liquidity, governance and resolvability
Passporting, cross-border services and regional access regimes
Equivalence, deference and reliance on home supervisors
Host safeguards for systemically important branches

modules.title: Cross-Border Crisis Cooperation and Resolution
modules.summary: How home and host authorities cooperate when a cross-border group comes under stress, from early warning and information sharing to crisis management groups and resolution.
objectives: Explain the FSB Key Attributes and cross-border resolution cooperation
Assess recovery and resolution planning for cross-border groups
Identify the conflicts of interest that arise between authorities in a crisis
syllabus: Crisis management groups and institution-specific cooperation agreements
Single and multiple point of entry resolution strategies
Ring-fencing incentives and host protection in stress
Coordinated communication with firms, markets and the public

modules.title: Making Cross-Border Cooperation Work
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining the practical obstacles to cooperation, how to escalate when cooperation breaks down, and a cross-border stress simulation.
objectives: Identify legal, mandate and resource obstacles to cooperation
Apply escalation options when cooperation breaks down
Produce a coordinated supervisory response to a cross-border scenario
syllabus: Legal barriers, differing mandates and resource asymmetry
Building trust and working relationships with counterpart authorities
Escalation routes, including standard-setter mechanisms
Workshop: simulation of a cross-border group under stress

related.title: Conduct, Culture and Behavioural Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module programme on assessing conduct risk and culture in firms, using behavioural insights, data and targeted supervisory interventions.

related.title: Consumer Protection and Financial Inclusion
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess product governance, fair value, disclosure, vulnerable customer treatment, complaints and financial inclusion.

related.title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.
